name: The Wheel
summary: Sell cash-secured puts until assigned, then sell covered calls on the assigned shares until called away, and repeat. Structurally sound but DIRECTLY CONFLICTS with the system's never-assign mandate.

legs.strike_rule: Phase 1: cash-secured put at delta -0.25 to -0.30
Phase 2 (only if assigned): covered call at delta 0.25-0.30, strike at or above the assigned cost basis

max_profit: Per cycle: put credit + call credit + (call strike - assignment price) x 100
max_loss: Full stock downside from the put strike, minus accumulated credits. In a sustained decline the wheel accumulates shares and losses at the same time.
breakevens: Rolling: assigned cost basis minus all credits collected to date

greeks.delta: +0.25 to +0.30 in the put phase; +0.70 to +0.75 in the covered call phase

when_to_use: For accounts that WANT to be assigned. This system does not. Either disable the wheel entirely, or run the modified no-assignment form described in the rules, which rolls instead of accepting assignment and therefore never reaches phase 2.
entry_rules: CONFLICT FLAG: the standard wheel requires accepting assignment. This system's mandate is never to be assigned. Do not run the standard form

Modified no-assignment form, if enabled: run only the cash-secured put phase, and when the put would otherwise be assigned, roll down and out for a credit instead. Phase 2 then only occurs if a roll fails and assignment happens anyway - treated as a breach, not a plan
Phase 1 gates identical to cash-secured-put: IVR > 30, delta -0.25 to -0.30, 30-45 DTE, cash >= strike x 100, credit >= 1% of strike per 30 days
Only on names the account would tolerate holding: ADV >= 2M, price $20-$150 (so a round lot fits inside 20% of equity), no leveraged or inverse ETFs
management_rules: Put phase: close at 50% of credit or 21 DTE
Roll down and out for a net credit when delta exceeds -0.50; maximum 2 rolls per cycle, then close
Call phase (only after an unintended assignment): sell a 0.25-0.30 delta call with a strike at or above the assignment price. Never write a call below cost basis just to collect a credit
Track cost basis net of every credit ever collected on the symbol; that number, not the raw assignment price, is the real breakeven
Stop the wheel on a symbol after 3 consecutive losing cycles or a 20% drawdown in the underlying
exit_rules: Put phase: close at 50% of credit, 21 DTE, or the 2.5x credit stop
NEVER-ASSIGN RULE: roll or close any short put at extrinsic < $0.10, delta > -0.85, or within 1.0% of the strike at 14:30 ET on expiration day; hard backstop 15:45 ET
Call phase: close at 50% of credit or 21 DTE; same never-assign triggers on the short call plus the pre-ex-dividend check
If an unintended assignment occurs, log it as a system breach, sell the shares or begin the covered-call phase per explicit human decision, and disable new wheel entries on that symbol until reviewed
assignment_risk: By design, the classic wheel EXPECTS assignment on both legs - which is precisely why it must be modified or disabled here. The put assigns shares to you; the call assigns them away.
buying_power: Put phase: strike x 100 in cash. Call phase: the shares themselves.
liquidity_needs: Both phases need OI >= 500 and spreads <= 8% of mid, since rolling is the core mechanic.
common_mistakes: Wheeling a stock in a downtrend and calling the accumulating losses income; writing calls below the assigned cost basis; running the standard wheel in a system whose core invariant is never to hold shares from assignment.
